newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW recess talks with no strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW recess talks with no strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp. and the United Auto Workers union adjourned labour contract negotiations for several hours early Monday and the UAW scheduled a news conference for 8:00 A.M. EST.

No strike had been called, despite the expiration of a midnight Sunday strike deadline set by the union. In a statement, UAW president Stephen Yokich and vice president Richard Shoemaker said they will discuss the status of the negotiations at the news conference at Solidarity House, the union's Detroit headquarters.
Members of the UAW's bargaining team began leaving GM's headquarters here with overnight bags shortly after 0200 EST Monday, but they declined to comment on the status of the talks.
"There has been no talk of a strike," said GM spokesman Gerry Holmes.
GM plans to resume the talks sometime after the UAW news conference is completed, but no specific time has been set.

There was speculation among some union officials Sunday night that Yokich may decide to have workers strike a few key plants rather than wage a broad national strike against the automaker close to the presidential election. The most likely plants would be those that build the automaker's high-profit full-size pickup trucks and sport/utility vehicles, including facilities in Janesville, Wis., Pontiac and Flint, Mich., and Fort Wayne, Ind.
